queries: WITH p AS (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB * 1.0 / HCT) AS r, AVG(PIC) AS pic FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID), a AS (SELECT AVG(r) AS m FROM p) SELECT AVG(p.pic) AS mean_avg_pic, AVG(p.r) AS mean_ratio, AVG(p.r - a.m) AS mean_excess FROM p CROSS JOIN a WHERE p.r > a.m

WITH p AS (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB) * 1.0 / AVG(HCT) AS r, AVG(PIC) AS pic FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID), a AS (SELECT AVG(r) AS m FROM p) SELECT AVG(p.pic) AS mean_avg_pic, AVG(p.r) AS mean_ratio, AVG(p.r - a.m) AS mean_excess FROM p CROSS JOIN a WHERE p.r > a.m

WITH r AS (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB * 1.0 / HCT) AS ratio FROM Laboratory WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL AND HCT IS NOT NULL AND HCT <> 0 GROUP BY ID), pic AS (SELECT ID, AVG(PIC) AS avg_pic FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID), g AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS m FROM r) SELECT AVG(pic.avg_pic) AS mean_avg_pic, AVG(r.ratio) AS mean_ratio, AVG(r.ratio - g.m) AS mean_excess FROM r JOIN pic ON pic.ID = r.ID CROSS JOIN g WHERE r.ratio > g.m

WITH r AS (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB) * 1.0 / AVG(HCT) AS ratio FROM Laboratory WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL AND HCT IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ID HAVING AVG(HCT) <> 0), pic AS (SELECT ID, AVG(PIC) AS avg_pic FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID), g AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS m FROM r) SELECT AVG(pic.avg_pic) AS mean_avg_pic, AVG(r.ratio) AS mean_ratio, AVG(r.ratio - g.m) AS mean_excess FROM r JOIN pic ON pic.ID = r.ID CROSS JOIN g WHERE r.ratio > g.m

WITH p AS (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB * 1.0 / NULLIF(HCT, 0)) AS ratio, AVG(PIC) AS avg_pic FROM Laboratory WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL AND HCT IS NOT NULL AND HCT <> 0 GROUP BY ID), g AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM p) SELECT AVG(p.avg_pic) AS mean_avg_pic, AVG(p.ratio) AS mean_ratio, AVG(p.ratio - g.avg_ratio) AS mean_excess FROM p CROSS JOIN g WHERE p.ratio > g.avg_ratio;

assumptions.assumption: A patient's ratio is the average of the row-level HGB/HCT ratios across their lab records, skipping rows where HGB or HCT is NULL (and HCT = 0).
The cross-patient average is the unweighted mean of the per-patient ratios, so each patient counts once.
A patient's average PIC is taken over all their lab rows, not just rows with a valid ratio. Patients whose PIC is always NULL are ignored in the final mean.
'Above average' means strictly greater than the average.

alternatives.interpretation: A patient's ratio is the ratio of their average HGB to their average HCT, rather than the average of row-level ratios.
alternatives.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB) * 1.0 / AVG(HCT) AS r, AVG(PIC) AS pic FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID), a AS (SELECT AVG(r) AS m FROM p) SELECT AVG(p.pic) AS mean_avg_pic, AVG(p.r) AS mean_ratio, AVG(p.r - a.m) AS mean_excess FROM p CROSS JOIN a WHERE p.r > a.m

assumptions.assumption: A patient's ratio is the average of the row-level HGB/HCT ratios over their lab rows where both values are non-null and HCT is non-zero.
The cross-patient average is the unweighted mean of the per-patient ratios (each patient counts once), not a mean over all lab rows.
A patient's average PIC is taken over all of their lab rows with non-null PIC; patients with no PIC values are excluded from the PIC mean but still count in the ratio means.

alternatives.interpretation: A patient's ratio is their average HGB divided by their average HCT (ratio of means) instead of the mean of row-level ratios.

assumptions.assumption: A patient's ratio is the average of HGB/HCT over their lab rows where both values are present and HCT is nonzero. The cross-patient average is the unweighted mean of the patient ratios, so each patient counts once.
A patient's average PIC is taken over the same rows used for the ratio (HGB and HCT present). Patients whose PIC is always NULL are ignored in the mean of average PIC.

alternatives.interpretation: A patient's ratio is their average HGB divided by their average HCT, instead of the average of per-row ratios.
